mmlu.description: A benchmark designed to rigorously evaluate multi-modal reasoning with explicit thinking traces. It includes a high-difficulty dataset spanning diverse reasoning types with symbolic depth and multi-hop demands.

gpqa.bmt_title: GPQA: A Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A Benchmark
gpqa.description: GPQA is a challenging multiple-choice question answering dataset written by domain experts in biology, physics, and chemistry. It is designed to be difficult even for highly skilled non-experts with unrestricted access to the internet (Google-proof), while domain experts can answer them with high accuracy.

humaneval.specs: Python functions with docstrings and unit tests
humaneval.description: A benchmark for evaluating the functional correctness of code generated by Large Language Models. It consists of programming problems that include a function signature, docstring, body, and unit tests.

math.item_count: Derived from GSM8K and MATH training sets
math.description: A dataset created for automatic process supervision. It assigns reward scores to each step of math problem solutions without requiring human annotation, derived from the GSM8K and MATH datasets. It is used to train PRMs for verification and reinforcement learning.

gsm8k.description: A dataset of high-quality linguistically diverse grade school math word problems. It is designed to support the task of question answering on basic mathematical problems that require multi-step reasoning.

mmmu.specs: Multimodal (Image/Screenshot), Multiple Choice (10 options), Vision-only input setting
mmmu.description: A robust version of the MMMU benchmark designed to rigorously assess true multimodal understanding. It filters out text-only answerable questions, augments candidate options to 10 choices, and introduces a vision-only input setting (screenshots) to test the integration of visual and textual information.

swe_bench.specs: Python codebases, GitHub issues/PRs, Docker execution environment
swe_bench.description: A benchmark for evaluating large language models on real-world software engineering issues collected from GitHub. It tasks agents with resolving issues (bugs/features) in popular Python repositories by generating patches that pass new tests.

truthfulqa.specs: Text questions (Multiple choice and Generation), CSV
truthfulqa.description: A benchmark to measure whether language models generate truthful answers to questions, focusing on imitative falsehoods and misconceptions.

ifeval.specs: Text-based, verifiable instructions (e.g., word count constraints, format requirements)
ifeval.description: A benchmark designed to evaluate the ability of Large Language Models (LLMs) to follow verifiable instructions, focusing on objective metrics rather than subjective human evaluation.

aime.specs: JSONL format; Text modality; Integer answers (0-999)
aime.description: A benchmark dataset consisting of 30 problems from the 2024 American Invitational Mathematics Examination (AIME I and II). It is widely used to evaluate the mathematical reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) on difficult, Olympiad-level problems.

healthbench_professional.description: An open-source benchmark designed to measure the performance and safety of large language models in healthcare. It consists of realistic multi-turn conversations between a model and an individual user or healthcare professional, evaluating responses against conversation-specific rubrics created by physicians. The benchmark covers diverse themes such as emergency referrals, context-seeking, and global health.

healthbench.description: An open-source benchmark designed to measure the performance and safety of large language models in healthcare. It consists of realistic multi-turn conversations between a model and an individual user or healthcare professional, evaluating responses against conversation-specific rubrics created by physicians. The benchmark covers diverse themes such as emergency referrals, context-seeking, and global health.

medqa_usmle.specs: Text (Question Answering), Multiple Choice (4 or 5 options)
medqa_usmle.description: A large-scale open-domain question answering dataset collected from professional medical board exams. The primary subset consists of questions from the United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE).

medmcqa.description: A large-scale multiple-choice question answering dataset designed to address real-world medical entrance exam questions (AIIMS & NEET PG) covering a wide range of medical subjects.

pubmedqa.description: A biomedical question answering dataset collected from PubMed abstracts. The task is to answer research questions with yes/no/maybe using the corresponding abstract context.

mmlu_clinical.description: A benchmark designed to rigorously evaluate multi-modal reasoning with explicit thinking traces. It includes a high-difficulty dataset spanning diverse reasoning types with symbolic depth and multi-hop demands.

medxpertqa.item_count: 4,460 questions (Text subset: 2,455; Multimodal subset: 2,005 questions with 2,839 images)
medxpertqa.specs: Text and Multimodal (Images + Structured Tables). Covers 17 medical specialties and 11 body systems. Format: Multiple-choice questions (10 options for Text, 5 for MM).
medxpertqa.description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate expert-level medical knowledge and advanced reasoning capabilities in AI models. It encompasses diverse real-world diagnostic scenarios, including highly specialized fields, and features both text-only and multimodal subsets. The multimodal subset integrates structured clinical data (e.g., patient records, tables) with medical images to simulate realistic clinical decision-making.

radbench.item_count: Includes 5 downstream tasks (Modality Recognition, Disease Diagnosis, VQA, Report Generation, Rationale Diagnosis)
radbench.description: A benchmark suite proposed alongside the Radiology Foundation Model (RadFM) to evaluate generalist medical AI capabilities. It assesses models on five diverse radiologic tasks using a large-scale multimodal dataset.

medxpertqa_text.item_count: 4,460 questions (Text subset: 2,455; Multimodal subset: 2,005 questions with 2,839 images)
medxpertqa_text.specs: Text and Multimodal (Images + Structured Tables). Covers 17 medical specialties and 11 body systems. Format: Multiple-choice questions (10 options for Text, 5 for MM).
medxpertqa_text.description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate expert-level medical knowledge and advanced reasoning capabilities in AI models. It encompasses diverse real-world diagnostic scenarios, including highly specialized fields, and features both text-only and multimodal subsets. The multimodal subset integrates structured clinical data (e.g., patient records, tables) with medical images to simulate realistic clinical decision-making.

medxpertqa_mm.item_count: 4,460 questions (Text subset: 2,455; Multimodal subset: 2,005 questions with 2,839 images)
medxpertqa_mm.specs: Text and Multimodal (Images + Structured Tables). Covers 17 medical specialties and 11 body systems. Format: Multiple-choice questions (10 options for Text, 5 for MM).
medxpertqa_mm.description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate expert-level medical knowledge and advanced reasoning capabilities in AI models. It encompasses diverse real-world diagnostic scenarios, including highly specialized fields, and features both text-only and multimodal subsets. The multimodal subset integrates structured clinical data (e.g., patient records, tables) with medical images to simulate realistic clinical decision-making.

ehrqa.description: A multi-modal question answering dataset focusing on medication-related queries. It contains QA pairs derived from both structured tables and unstructured discharge summaries in MIMIC-III, designed to improve QA using cross-modal context.

medqa_4opt.specs: Text (Question Answering), Multiple Choice (4 or 5 options)
medqa_4opt.description: A large-scale open-domain question answering dataset collected from professional medical board exams. The primary subset consists of questions from the United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE).

care_qa.description: A dataset derived from the Spanish Specialized Healthcare Training (FSE) exams (MIR, EIR, etc.). It serves as a benchmark for medical question answering in Spanish.

omnimedvqa.specs: 12 Modalities (CT, MRI, X-ray, etc.), QA pairs
omnimedvqa.description: A comprehensive medical Visual Question Answering benchmark collected from 73 different medical datasets, covering 12 modalities and over 20 anatomical regions. Designed to evaluate Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs).

brats.bmt_title: BraTS (Multimodal Brain Tumor Image Segmentation Benchmark)
brats.specs: Multi-modal MRI (T1, T1ce, T2, FLAIR), NIfTI format
brats.description: A long-running benchmark challenge for the segmentation of brain tumors (gliomas) in multimodal magnetic resonance imaging scans.

wmdp_bio.bmt_title: WMDP (Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy) Benchmark
wmdp_bio.specs: Text (Multiple Choice Questions); Domains: Biosecurity, Cybersecurity, Chemical Security
wmdp_bio.description: A dataset of multiple-choice questions serving as a proxy measure for hazardous knowledge in biosecurity, cybersecurity, and chemical security. It is designed to evaluate LLM unlearning methods and malicious use risks.

wmdp_chem.bmt_title: WMDP (Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy) Benchmark
wmdp_chem.specs: Text (Multiple Choice Questions); Domains: Biosecurity, Cybersecurity, Chemical Security
wmdp_chem.description: A dataset of multiple-choice questions serving as a proxy measure for hazardous knowledge in biosecurity, cybersecurity, and chemical security. It is designed to evaluate LLM unlearning methods and malicious use risks.

vct_virology.specs: Multimodal (Text + Images), Multiple-Choice (Single and Multiple Select)
vct_virology.description: A multimodal benchmark measuring the capability of Large Language Models (LLMs) to troubleshoot complex virology laboratory protocols. It covers fundamental, tacit, and visual knowledge essential for practical work in virology.

biolp_bench.description: Evaluates the proficiency of language models in finding and correcting mistakes in biological laboratory protocols. Unlike multiple-choice benchmarks, it uses open-ended questions where models must identify failure-causing errors injected into real-world protocols.

moleculenet_avg.specs: Molecular structures (SMILES/graphs), regression and classification tasks
moleculenet_avg.description: A benchmark for molecular machine learning, curating multiple public datasets to test methods on molecular properties including quantum mechanics, physical chemistry, biophysics, and physiology.

tdc_admet.description: A large collection of AI-ready datasets and tasks for drug discovery and development, covering small molecules, biologics, and gene editing across various stages of the therapeutic pipeline.

vqamed_2024.description: A dataset created for the ImageCLEF 2019 VQA-Med task. It focuses on four categories of questions: Modality, Plane, Organ System, and Abnormality, derived from radiology images.

med_halt.specs: Text modality; includes False Confidence Test (FCT) and None of the Above (NOTA) test formats.
med_halt.description: A benchmark dataset designed specifically to evaluate and reduce hallucinations in medical LLMs. It includes reasoning and memory-based hallucination tests to assess problem-solving and information retrieval abilities.

medhallu.specs: Medical QA, binary hallucination detection, difficulty levels
medhallu.description: A comprehensive benchmark specifically designed for detecting medical hallucinations in LLMs. It contains QA pairs derived from PubMedQA with systematically generated hallucinations classified by difficulty (Easy, Medium, Hard).

medsafetybench.specs: Text (harmful queries and safe response pairs)
medsafetybench.description: The first benchmark dataset designed to measure the medical safety of LLMs based on the Principles of Medical Ethics. It includes harmful medical requests and safe responses to evaluate and fine-tune models for safety while preserving medical performance.

patientsafebench.specs: Text (patient-oriented queries across 5 critical policy categories: Harmful Advice, Misdiagnosis, Unlicensed Practice, etc.)
patientsafebench.description: A patient-focused benchmark designed to evaluate the safety of Large Language Models (LLMs) in the medical domain. It tests critical safety policies to measure how well models avoid harmful, misleading, unlicensed, or discriminatory responses when interacting with non-medical users.

csedb_safety.description: A medical risk scoring benchmark that evaluates LLMs on both safety and effectiveness in clinical scenarios. It encompasses 30 criteria including critical illness recognition and medication safety to provide a standardized metric for clinical risk exposure.

csedb_effectiveness.description: A medical risk scoring benchmark that evaluates LLMs on both safety and effectiveness in clinical scenarios. It encompasses 30 criteria including critical illness recognition and medication safety to provide a standardized metric for clinical risk exposure.

medic_eval.description: A multimodal empathy dataset collected from face-to-face psychological counseling sessions. It is annotated for empathy mechanisms including expression of experience, emotional reaction, and cognitive reaction.

rexrank_radgraph_f1.description: A dataset of entities and relations extracted from radiology reports (MIMIC-CXR and CheXpert). It provides a schema and annotations for developing information extraction models for radiology text.

chexpert_f1.specs: Frontal and lateral chest radiographs, 14 observations with uncertainty labels
chexpert_f1.description: A large dataset of chest radiographs with uncertainty labels and radiologist-labeled reference standard evaluation sets, designed for automated interpretation.

vqa_rad.specs: Images (CT, MRI, X-ray), Text (Open-ended, Yes/No questions)
vqa_rad.description: A manually curated dataset of clinically generated visual questions and answers about radiology images. It is designed to evaluate VQA models on real-world clinical questions, distinguishing it from larger, automatically generated datasets.

slake_vqa.bmt_title: SLAKE: A Semantically-Labeled Knowledge-Enhanced Dataset for Medical Visual Question Answering
slake_vqa.specs: Bilingual (English/Chinese), Modalities: Image (CT, MRI, X-Ray) and Text. Formats: JSON, JPG. Includes semantic segmentation masks and bounding boxes.
slake_vqa.description: A large-scale bilingual (English and Chinese) benchmark dataset for Medical Visual Question Answering (Med-VQA). It contains radiology images (CT, MRI, X-Ray) with comprehensive semantic annotations (masks, bounding boxes) and a structured medical knowledge graph to facilitate both visual and knowledge-based reasoning.

path_vqa.description: A dataset designed for medical visual question answering (VQA) in pathology. It contains question-answer pairs generated from pathology textbooks and digital libraries, including both open-ended and binary (yes/no) questions.

afrimed_qa_mcq.specs: Includes 4,000+ expert Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs), 1,200+ Open-Ended Short Answer Questions (SAQs), and 10,000 Consumer Queries (CQs). Covers 32 medical specialties across 16 African countries.
afrimed_qa_mcq.description: A large-scale Pan-African, multi-specialty medical Question-Answering (QA) benchmark dataset designed to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) in the context of African healthcare. The dataset aims to address the underrepresentation of African health data in LLM training and evaluation, covering diverse geographic and clinical contexts.

afrimed_qa_saq.specs: Includes 4,000+ expert Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs), 1,200+ Open-Ended Short Answer Questions (SAQs), and 10,000 Consumer Queries (CQs). Covers 32 medical specialties across 16 African countries.
afrimed_qa_saq.description: A large-scale Pan-African, multi-specialty medical Question-Answering (QA) benchmark dataset designed to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) in the context of African healthcare. The dataset aims to address the underrepresentation of African health data in LLM training and evaluation, covering diverse geographic and clinical contexts.

mimic_iv_sepsis_auc.description: A freely accessible electronic health record dataset containing de-identified clinical data of patients admitted to the ICU and Emergency Department at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. It includes vital signs, laboratory measurements, medications, and free-text clinical notes.

mimic_aki_mortality.description: A freely accessible electronic health record dataset containing de-identified clinical data of patients admitted to the ICU and Emergency Department at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. It includes vital signs, laboratory measurements, medications, and free-text clinical notes.

mimic_iv_readmit.description: A freely accessible electronic health record dataset containing de-identified clinical data of patients admitted to the ICU and Emergency Department at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. It includes vital signs, laboratory measurements, medications, and free-text clinical notes.

openai_healthbench_hard.description: An open-source benchmark designed to measure the performance and safety of large language models in healthcare. It consists of realistic multi-turn conversations between a model and an individual user or healthcare professional, evaluating responses against conversation-specific rubrics created by physicians. The benchmark covers diverse themes such as emergency referrals, context-seeking, and global health.

medhelm.description: A holistic evaluation framework for assessing Large Language Models (LLMs) on medical tasks. It utilizes a clinician-validated taxonomy spanning various categories like clinical note generation and decision support.

medhelm_clin_dec.description: A holistic evaluation framework for assessing Large Language Models (LLMs) on medical tasks. It utilizes a clinician-validated taxonomy spanning various categories like clinical note generation and decision support.

medhelm_admin.description: A holistic evaluation framework for assessing Large Language Models (LLMs) on medical tasks. It utilizes a clinician-validated taxonomy spanning various categories like clinical note generation and decision support.

medhelm_note_gen.description: A holistic evaluation framework for assessing Large Language Models (LLMs) on medical tasks. It utilizes a clinician-validated taxonomy spanning various categories like clinical note generation and decision support.

medhelm_patient_comm.description: A holistic evaluation framework for assessing Large Language Models (LLMs) on medical tasks. It utilizes a clinician-validated taxonomy spanning various categories like clinical note generation and decision support.

medhelm_research.description: A holistic evaluation framework for assessing Large Language Models (LLMs) on medical tasks. It utilizes a clinician-validated taxonomy spanning various categories like clinical note generation and decision support.

agentclinic_medqa.description: A multimodal agent benchmark simulating clinical environments to evaluate LLMs. It features doctor-patient interaction simulations where the doctor agent must uncover diagnoses through dialogue and active data collection. Includes AgentClinic-MedQA and AgentClinic-NEJM environments.

agentclinic_nejm.description: A multimodal agent benchmark simulating clinical environments to evaluate LLMs. It features doctor-patient interaction simulations where the doctor agent must uncover diagnoses through dialogue and active data collection. Includes AgentClinic-MedQA and AgentClinic-NEJM environments.

medagentbench.specs: Text (EHR data, clinical notes), FHIR-compliant environment interactions
medagentbench.description: A realistic virtual EHR environment designed to benchmark medical Large Language Model (LLM) agents. It evaluates agents on 100 patient-specific clinically-derived tasks including information retrieval, diagnosis, and treatment planning within a FHIR-compliant interactive environment.

multimedqa.item_count: 7 datasets total (includes MedQA, MedMCQA, PubMedQA, LiveQA, MedicationQA, MMLU-Clinical, HealthSearchQA)
multimedqa.description: A benchmark suite combining six existing open question answering datasets (including MedQA, MedMCQA, PubMedQA) and a new dataset 'HealthSearchQA' of consumer medical questions, designed to evaluate Large Language Models in the medical domain.

medqa_vals_ai.specs: Text (Question Answering), Multiple Choice (4 or 5 options)
medqa_vals_ai.description: A large-scale open-domain question answering dataset collected from professional medical board exams. The primary subset consists of questions from the United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE).

medmnist_v2.description: A large-scale MNIST-like collection of standardized biomedical images, designed to be a lightweight benchmark for 2D and 3D biomedical image classification. It covers primary data modalities (e.g., X-ray, OCT, Ultrasound, CT, EM) and diverse tasks (binary/multi-class, ordinal regression, multi-label).

ehrnoteqa.specs: Text (Clinical Discharge Summaries); Open-ended and Multi-choice QA; 8 Clinical Topics
ehrnoteqa.description: A benchmark built on MIMIC-IV EHR for evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) in clinical settings. It consists of question-answer pairs linked to distinct patients' discharge summaries. Unlike previous benchmarks, it focuses on multi-document reasoning where questions often require information from multiple discharge summaries. The dataset includes both open-ended and multi-choice formats, with questions generated by GPT-4 and manually refined by clinicians to ensure relevance.

echobench_med.description: A benchmark to systematically evaluate sycophancy in Medical Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs), assessing how models handle biased inputs in medical contexts.

dermabench.specs: Image + Text (VQA, Hierarchical Questions), Fitzpatrick Skin Types I-VI
dermabench.description: A clinician-annotated dermatology VQA benchmark built on the Diverse Dermatology Images (DDI) dataset. It evaluates models on diagnostic diversity, demographic fairness, and precise labeling using a hierarchical annotation schema.

dermavqa_das.description: An extension of the DermaVQA dataset that supports closed-ended question answering and dermatological lesion segmentation. It introduces the Dermatology Assessment Schema (DAS) for structured assessment.

medrepbench.description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) on structured medical report interpretation. It consists of de-identified real-world medical reports, including examination and laboratory reports, spanning diverse departments and acquisition formats (photos, screenshots, electronic documents).

pathmcqa.description: A multiple-choice question answering dataset for pathology, derived from multiple sources. It presents questions related to identification, grading, and subtyping of cancers (breast, cervical, prostate) based on pathology visual data.

ukbob.description: The largest labeled dataset of body organs, utilizing UK Biobank MRI data with automated labeling and manual validation for generalizable 3D medical image segmentation.

histai_wsi.specs: Whole Slide Images (WSI), Clinical Metadata, Multi-organ
histai_wsi.description: An open-source, large-scale whole slide image dataset designed to address the lack of scale and diversity in public pathology resources. It includes extensive clinical metadata, detailed pathological annotations, and standardized diagnostic coding across various tissue types. The dataset is intended for pre-training foundation models and benchmarking computational pathology tasks.

beetle_seg.specs: Whole Slide Images (WSI), Pixel-level Semantic Segmentation Masks
beetle_seg.description: A multicentric dataset for training and benchmarking breast cancer semantic segmentation in H&E slides. It includes biopsies and resections from multiple clinical centers and scanners, covering all molecular subtypes and histological grades. Annotations include invasive epithelium, non-invasive epithelium, necrosis, and other tissues.

spider_path.item_count: Large-scale patch collection (exact count varies by subset)
spider_path.description: A comprehensive multi-organ supervised pathology dataset designed to provide expert annotations and strong baseline models for patch-level analysis. It serves as a large-scale resource for training and validating supervised learning models across different tissue types.

clinicalbench.description: A benchmark built to compare LLMs against traditional machine learning models in clinical prediction tasks. It focuses on tabular clinical data prediction scenarios such as length-of-stay, mortality, and readmission prediction.

bioprobench.description: A comprehensive benchmark for biological protocol understanding and reasoning, grounded in a large corpus of human-written protocols (BioProCorpus). It evaluates LLMs on tasks demanding deep reasoning and safety awareness in wet-lab contexts.

long_form_virology.description: A task-based agentic evaluation designed to test the end-to-end completion of complex pathogen acquisition processes, including workflow design and laboratory protocols. It is used to assess biological risks in frontier models.

msd_decathlon.specs: CT and MRI; NIfTI format; 3D volumes
msd_decathlon.description: A comprehensive benchmark comprising 10 different segmentation tasks to test the generalizability of algorithms. Tumor-related tasks include Brain (glioma), Liver (tumor), Lung (cancer), Pancreas (tumor), and Colon (cancer).

brats_2023.bmt_title: BraTS (Multimodal Brain Tumor Image Segmentation Benchmark)
brats_2023.specs: Multi-modal MRI (T1, T1ce, T2, FLAIR), NIfTI format
brats_2023.description: A long-running benchmark challenge for the segmentation of brain tumors (gliomas) in multimodal magnetic resonance imaging scans.

isic_2020.bmt_title: ISIC 2018: Skin Lesion Analysis Towards Melanoma Detection
isic_2020.specs: Dermoscopic images (JPEG) with binary segmentation masks (PNG). Modality: Image (Skin).
isic_2020.description: A large-scale dataset for skin lesion analysis, including lesion segmentation, attribute detection, and disease classification. It serves as a benchmark for melanoma detection.

hyper_kvasir.specs: Images (JPEG), Videos, Segmentation masks (1,000 images), Class labels (23 classes)
hyper_kvasir.description: A large-scale comprehensive dataset for gastrointestinal endoscopy. It includes images and videos covering anatomical landmarks, pathological findings, and normal findings, designed for classification, segmentation, and detection tasks.

medcalc_bench.description: A dataset designed to evaluate the medical calculation capabilities of LLMs. It includes rule-based and equation-based calculation tasks derived from real-world clinical calculators, requiring models to extract attributes from patient notes and perform arithmetic.

meddialog.description: A large-scale medical dialogue dataset containing conversations between doctors and patients. It includes two subsets: a Chinese dataset (MedDialog-CN) and an English dataset (MedDialog-EN), covering a wide range of medical specialties.

meddialog_rubrics.description: A benchmark and evaluation framework specifically designed to assess the multi-turn diagnostic reasoning and safety capabilities of medical LLMs. It utilizes a multi-agent system to synthesize realistic patient cases and employs fine-grained rubrics to evaluate information gathering, diagnostic accuracy, and hallucination risks.

climedbench_cn.specs: Chinese language, Real-world medical reports, 14 scenarios
climedbench_cn.description: A large-scale Chinese benchmark for evaluating medical LLMs in clinical scenarios. It comprises questions derived from real-world medical reports and examination exercises, covering 14 expert-guided core clinical scenarios.

multimed.specs: Modalities: 10 types including Text, Radiology (OCT, X-ray, CT, MRI), Pathology, Genomics, Protein, EEG
multimed.description: A massively multimodal benchmark designed to evaluate large-scale learning across a wide spectrum of medical modalities. It covers tasks like disease prognosis and protein structure prediction.

openi_iu.specs: Frontal and lateral X-ray images, associated radiology reports (XML)
openi_iu.description: A public chest X-ray dataset collected from the Indiana University hospital network, widely used for report generation benchmarks.

padchest_gr.specs: Chest X-rays, Reports (En/Es), Bounding box grounding
padchest_gr.description: A large-scale bilingual (Spanish/English) grounded radiology reporting benchmark dataset derived from PadChest, featuring bounding box annotations for findings.

pharmkg.specs: Knowledge Graph (Nodes: Genes, Drugs, Diseases; Edges: 29 relation types).
pharmkg.description: A multi-relational, attributed biomedical knowledge graph benchmark linking genes, drugs, and diseases for data mining and link prediction tasks.

roco_v2.specs: Radiology images, Captions, UMLS Concepts, Modality labels
roco_v2.description: A large-scale multimodal medical imaging dataset consisting of radiology images and caption pairs extracted from PMC Open Access articles. Designed for image captioning, retrieval, and multimodal learning.

rsna_pneumonia.specs: Chest X-ray images, Bounding box annotations
rsna_pneumonia.description: A dataset and challenge for detecting lung opacities (pneumonia) in chest radiographs. It provides bounding box annotations for positive cases.

tcga_reports.specs: Text (Pathology reports, linkable to TCGA WSIs)
tcga_reports.description: A machine-readable corpus of pathology reports derived from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). While primarily a text resource, it links to publicly available TCGA images, serving as a benchmark for text-based AI models and report generation when paired with image data.

vindr_cxr.specs: DICOM images, bounding box annotations for 22 local findings, 6 global disease labels
vindr_cxr.description: An open dataset of chest X-rays with radiologist annotations for the classification of common thoracic diseases and localization of critical findings.

ruijin_pd.bmt_title: Foundation-Model-Driven Parkinson's Disease Auto Diagnosis Challenge (Ruijin-PD)
ruijin_pd.specs: Multi-parametric MRI (T1WI, QSM, NM-MRI) with segmentation masks for 7 anatomical structures
ruijin_pd.description: A benchmark dataset designed for the MICCAI 2025 challenge, specifically focusing on using foundation models for Parkinson's Disease diagnosis and Deep Gray Matter (DGM) segmentation. It provides high-quality annotations for anatomical structures often difficult to segment.

toxicchat_med.specs: Text (User-AI conversation pairs), annotated for toxicity and jailbreaking
toxicchat_med.description: A benchmark based on real-world user-AI conversations from an open-source chatbot, designed to evaluate toxicity detection and jailbreaking attempts in realistic interactive settings.

live_dr_bench.specs: JSON format; Domains: Scientific (datasets, materials, prior art) and World Events; Metrics: Precision, Recall, F1 score on claim discovery
live_dr_bench.description: A diverse and challenging benchmark designed to characterize and evaluate 'deep research' tasks, defined by high concept fan-out and reasoning-intensive exploration rather than just long-form output. It separates reasoning challenges from surface-level report generation using an intermediate claim representation.

chexpert_plus.specs: Chest X-ray images, Text reports, Demographics
chexpert_plus.description: An augmented version of the CheXpert dataset that includes the original text radiology reports, patient demographics, and additional image formats, enabling text-based and multimodal research.

ms_cxr.specs: Longitudinal Chest X-rays, Temporal labels, Sentence pairs
ms_cxr.description: A multi-modal benchmark for evaluating biomedical vision-language processing models on temporal tasks, specifically measuring disease progression and temporal-semantic similarity in radiology reports.

chest_imagenome.specs: Multimodal (Image + Text + Structured Labels); Bounding boxes, Scene graphs
chest_imagenome.description: A dataset derived from MIMIC-CXR that provides scene graphs, bounding box annotations for anatomical locations, and consistent relations between findings and anatomy. Used for benchmarking grounding and localization capabilities in medical VLMs.

drive_retinal.bmt_title: DRIVE (Digital Retinal Images for Vessel Extraction)
drive_retinal.specs: Color fundus images, 565x584 pixels, binary vessel masks
drive_retinal.description: One of the most established benchmarks for retinal vessel segmentation. The images were acquired from a diabetic retinopathy screening program in the Netherlands. It contains 40 images divided into training and test sets.

rsna_brain_hemorrhage.description: A massive dataset comprised of de-identified head CT scans, created for the 2019 RSNA AI Challenge. It serves as a benchmark for detecting and classifying five subtypes of intracranial hemorrhage: intraparenchymal, intraventricular, subarachnoid, subdural, and epidural.

sam3_pcs_image.description: A fully volumetric adaptation of the Segment Anything Model (SAM) for 3D medical image segmentation. While general-purpose, it is a primary benchmark for 3D tumor segmentation tasks, evaluating performance on datasets like BraTS and KiTS.

sam3_pcs_video.description: A fully volumetric adaptation of the Segment Anything Model (SAM) for 3D medical image segmentation. While general-purpose, it is a primary benchmark for 3D tumor segmentation tasks, evaluating performance on datasets like BraTS and KiTS.

medsam3_2d_avg.bmt_title: MedSAM: Segment Anything in Medical Images
medsam3_2d_avg.item_count: 1.5 million+ masks from 1 million+ images (30+ datasets)
medsam3_2d_avg.specs: 2D and 3D Medical Images (CT, MRI, X-ray, Ultrasound, Pathology)
medsam3_2d_avg.description: The first large-scale adaptation of SAM for medical imaging. It created a massive dataset to fine-tune SAM, serving as the baseline for almost all subsequent 'Segment Any Tumor' research.

lits_3d.specs: 3D CT scans (NIfTI format). Modality: Medical Imaging (CT).
lits_3d.description: A benchmark dataset for automatic segmentation of liver and liver tumors in CT scans, aiming to compare different algorithms' performance on diverse clinical data.

isles_2024.specs: Multi-modal MRI (DWI, ADC, FLAIR). Modality: Medical Imaging (MRI).
isles_2024.description: A multi-center MRI dataset for the segmentation of acute to sub-acute ischemic stroke lesions, featuring high variability in lesion size and location.

med80_avg.specs: CT and MRI; NIfTI format; 3D volumes
med80_avg.description: A comprehensive benchmark comprising 10 different segmentation tasks to test the generalizability of algorithms. Tumor-related tasks include Brain (glioma), Liver (tumor), Lung (cancer), Pancreas (tumor), and Colon (cancer).

ct_3d_seg_avg.specs: CAD furniture models, 5,000+ rooms, 20,000+ photo-realistic rendered images, high-res textures
ct_3d_seg_avg.description: A large-scale, richly-annotated repository of 3D furniture shapes with high-resolution textures. It is designed to support 3D modeling from images, texture recovery, and interior design understanding.

gift_eval_ts.description: A benchmark designed to evaluate zero-shot forecasting capabilities of foundation models. It features a diverse collection of datasets spanning multiple domains and frequencies to prevent test data leakage.

fets_2_brats.specs: Brain MRI, Multi-center (global), Multi-vendor, Tumor segmentation
fets_2_brats.description: The FeTS dataset is constructed to benchmark federated learning algorithms for brain tumor segmentation. It aggregates MRI scans from multiple institutions globally, representing a highly heterogeneous data distribution in terms of scanners, protocols, and patient demographics, making it a key benchmark for multi-center generalization.

fets_2024_aggregation.specs: Brain MRI, Multi-center (global), Multi-vendor, Tumor segmentation
fets_2024_aggregation.description: The FeTS dataset is constructed to benchmark federated learning algorithms for brain tumor segmentation. It aggregates MRI scans from multiple institutions globally, representing a highly heterogeneous data distribution in terms of scanners, protocols, and patient demographics, making it a key benchmark for multi-center generalization.

matharena_project_euler.description: A project-level benchmark for unit test generation covering Python, Java, and JavaScript. Unlike function-level benchmarks, it focuses on generating tests within the context of moderate-sized, high-quality projects.

swe_bench_pro.specs: Multilingual (Python, Java, Go, JS, etc.), Docker-based, Enterprise/Commercial & Open Source splits
swe_bench_pro.description: An enterprise-level benchmark featuring 1,865 complex, long-horizon software engineering tasks sourced from 41 actively maintained repositories. It is designed to be significantly more challenging than the original SWE-bench, incorporating multi-file edits and substantial code modifications. This dataset was a primary evaluation target for the 'Live-SWE-agent' paper.

caibench.specs: Multi-modal evaluation suite including text-based knowledge questions, interactive CTF environments, and privacy assessment modules.
caibench.description: A meta-benchmark framework designed to evaluate the offensive, defensive, knowledge-based, and privacy-preserving capabilities of cybersecurity AI agents. It integrates multiple evaluation styles including Jeopardy-style CTFs, Attack & Defense CTFs, and Cyber Range exercises.

jailbreakbench.description: An open robustness benchmark for jailbreaking LLMs, featuring a repository of artifacts, a dataset of misuse behaviors (JBB-Behaviors), and a standardized evaluation framework.

lab_bench_bio.specs: Multiple-choice questions across 8 categories (LitQA2, DbQA, SuppQA, FigQA, TableQA, ProtocolQA, SeqQA, Cloning Scenarios); Modalities include text, technical images, and biological sequences (DNA/protein)
lab_bench_bio.description: LAB-Bench is a large-scale evaluation dataset designed to measure the capabilities of AI systems for practical biology research. Unlike textbook-style benchmarks, it focuses on real-world tasks such as literature search, protocol planning, data analysis, and the interpretation of figures and biological sequences. It includes difficult 'Cloning Scenarios' that simulate complex molecular cloning workflows.

redbench.bmt_title: RedBench: A Universal Dataset for Comprehensive Red Teaming of Large Language Models
redbench.specs: Text (Attack and Refusal prompts), 22 risk categories, 19 domains
redbench.description: A universal dataset aggregating 37 benchmark datasets for red teaming Large Language Models (LLMs). It employs a standardized taxonomy with 22 risk categories and 19 domains to enable consistent and comprehensive evaluations of LLM vulnerabilities against adversarial prompts.

automonitor_bench.specs: QA, code generation, and reasoning tasks with paired misbehavior instances.
automonitor_bench.description: A benchmark designed to evaluate the reliability of LLM-based misbehavior monitors. It includes specific categories for 'Specification Gaming', where models exploit loopholes in evaluation criteria. The dataset provides ground-truth annotations to measure detection rates of such behaviors.

enkrypt_cbrn.github_link: Not released publicly (Private to prevent misuse)
enkrypt_cbrn.specs: Text prompts; Domains: Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear
enkrypt_cbrn.description: A comprehensive evaluation dataset designed to assess CBRN safety vulnerabilities in frontier LLMs, consisting of novel prompts and a subset of the FORTRESS benchmark.

impossiblebench.item_count: Hundreds of mutated coding tasks (derived from LiveCodeBench/SWE-bench)
impossiblebench.specs: Code generation tasks with mutated/conflicting unit tests.
impossiblebench.description: A framework for systematically measuring LLM agents' propensity to exploit test cases ('reward hacking') rather than following specifications. It creates 'impossible' variants of coding tasks from existing benchmarks (like LiveCodeBench and SWE-bench) by mutating unit tests to conflict with the natural language description, such that passing the test requires ignoring the specification.

cuaharm.specs: Sandboxed Environment, Text/Code Interaction; Categories: Credential Theft, Privilege Escalation, Network Exploitation, etc.
cuaharm.description: A benchmark designed to evaluate the misuse risks of Computer-Using Agents (CUAs). It measures agents' success rates in executing malicious tasks such as disabling firewalls, credential theft, and network exploitation in a sandboxed environment.

excytin_bench.specs: Text (SQL queries), Log Data; Environment: MySQL Docker container with Microsoft Sentinel logs
excytin_bench.description: The first benchmark to evaluate LLM agents on Cyber Threat Investigation. It provides a realistic environment with 57 log tables and 8 multi-stage attacks, requiring agents to query logs, follow evidence chains, and answer investigation questions.

pandabench.specs: JSON/CSV containing attack-defense interaction traces, ASR scores, and judge evaluations. Inputs based on JBB-Behaviors (100 harmful prompts).
pandabench.description: A comprehensive benchmark dataset evaluating Large Language Model (LLM) safety against jailbreaking attacks. It is built upon the PandaGuard framework and captures the interactions between 49 LLMs, 19 attack algorithms (including GCG, AutoDAN, PAIR), and 12 defense mechanisms (such as PerplexityFilter, SmoothLLM). The dataset focuses on the Attack Success Rate (ASR) and includes evaluation traces from multiple judge models.

ajailbench.item_count: 1,495 base adversarial audio prompts; Extended AJailBench-APT+ dataset available
ajailbench.specs: Audio (WAV/MP3), Text (JSONL format for prompts/responses), Python 3.10+
ajailbench.description: A comprehensive benchmark specifically designed to evaluate jailbreak vulnerabilities in Large Audio-Language Models (LAMs). It includes a base dataset of adversarial audio prompts derived from policy-violating text categories and an extended dataset generated using the Audio Perturbation Toolkit (APT) which applies time, frequency, and mixing domain perturbations.

jalmbench.specs: Audio files, Text prompts, Supports 12 ALM architectures
jalmbench.description: A large-scale benchmark for assessing the safety of Audio Language Models against jailbreak attacks. It standardizes the evaluation of 12 mainstream ALMs using both text-transferred and audio-originated attack methods, as well as defense strategies.

multi_audiojail.item_count: derived from 520 AdvBench prompts x 5 languages x accent variations
multi_audiojail.description: A framework and dataset designed to exploit multilingual and multi-accent vulnerabilities in Audio LLMs. It contains adversarially perturbed audio prompts across five languages and various accents to demonstrate how linguistic variations amplify attack success.

safepath.item_count: Derived from WildJailbreak (approx. 262k samples total, SafePath uses a harmful subset)
safepath.specs: Text (Harmful Prompts, Safety Primers, Reasoning Chains)
safepath.description: A dataset and alignment method designed to prevent harmful reasoning in Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) like DeepSeek-R1. The method fine-tunes models to emit a short 'Safety Primer' (e.g., 8 tokens) at the start of reasoning when encountering harmful prompts. The associated 'Safety Trigger set' is derived from the WildJailbreak dataset, containing harmful or adversarial prompts paired with safety primers to guide the model's Chain-of-Thought (CoT) towards safety without degrading reasoning performance on standard tasks.

omnisafebench_mm.description: A unified benchmark and toolbox for multimodal jailbreak attack-defense evaluation, covering 9 major risk domains and 50 fine-grained categories.

cyberteam_blue.bmt_title: CyberTeam: Benchmarking LLM-Assisted Blue Teaming via Standardized Threat Hunting
cyberteam_blue.specs: Threat hunting workflow tasks, embodied environment integration
cyberteam_blue.description: A benchmark designed to guide and evaluate LLMs in blue team threat hunting practices. It models realistic threat-hunting workflows by capturing dependencies among analytical tasks from threat attribution to incident response, using embodied functions.

purple_team_cyber.specs: Structured logs including attack events, defense responses, system logs, and network traffic metrics
purple_team_cyber.description: A synthetic collection designed to simulate collaborative cybersecurity exercises, integrating offensive (Red Team) and defensive (Blue Team) strategies. It includes records of attack events, defense responses, system logs, and network traffic.

alert_safety.description: A comprehensive benchmark for assessing LLM safety through red teaming, utilizing a fine-grained risk taxonomy to identify vulnerabilities and inform improvements.

primevul.description: A dataset for vulnerability detection that combines and reconstructs existing datasets with accurate labels and chronological splits to minimize data contamination. It aims to evaluate code language models in realistic settings.

injecagent.description: A benchmark for assessing indirect prompt injection attacks in tool-integrated LLM agents, featuring test cases across diverse user tools and domains to evaluate agent vulnerability.

pint_benchmark.description: A neutral benchmark for evaluating prompt injection detection systems, containing a mix of public datasets, proprietary injections, and jailbreaks to test false positives and negatives.

agentsmith_inf.item_count: Simulates up to 1 million agents; Uses subsets of ArtBench and AdvBench
agentsmith_inf.specs: Multimodal (Image + Text); Adversarial Attacks; Multi-agent simulation code
agentsmith_inf.description: A benchmark and simulation framework for evaluating 'infectious jailbreak' risks in multi-agent systems. It demonstrates how a single adversarial image can compromise an entire system of multimodal agents (e.g., LLaVA-1.5) exponentially fast. The benchmark typically uses ArtBench for image pools and AdvBench for target harmful behaviors.

jailbreakv_28k.specs: 20,000 text-based transfer attacks, 8,000 image-based attacks; text-image pairs
jailbreakv_28k.description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to assess the transferability of jailbreak attacks from LLMs to Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). It evaluates alignment robustness against text-based and image-based attacks.

browserart.specs: Harmful behaviors targeting 40 synthetic websites (hosted locally) and real websites
browserart.description: A red teaming test suite designed for browser agents, consisting of harmful behaviors aimed at synthetic and real websites. It highlights the safety gap between refusal-trained LLMs and their agentic counterparts in browser environments.

cybersec_eval3.item_count: 1,916 prompts (instruct dataset), plus other test suites
cybersec_eval3.specs: Text prompts, code snippets; Covers Prompt Injection, Insecure Code Generation (50 CWEs), Interpreter Abuse
cybersec_eval3.description: A comprehensive benchmark suite from Meta to quantify LLM security risks and capabilities, including prompt injection, code interpreter abuse, and insecure code generation. It evaluates models against OWASP-style vulnerabilities and measures the safety-utility tradeoff.

secure_code_v2.specs: JSON format; 11 programming languages; 4-turn conversational structure; Grounded in CVEs
secure_code_v2.description: A rigorously validated dataset of security-focused coding examples designed to train security-aware AI code generation models. Every example is grounded in real-world security incidents (CVEs) and covers the complete OWASP Top 10:2025 categories.

llmail_inject.description: A dataset resulting from a realistic adaptive prompt injection challenge simulating attacks on an LLM-based email assistant, including diverse attack strategies like obfuscation and social engineering.

ricota_kr_redteam.description: RICoTA (Red-teaming of In-the-wild Conversation with Test Attempts) is a Korean red teaming dataset designed to evaluate the safety of social chatbots. It consists of real-world user dialogues that contain jailbreaking attempts, such as 'taming' the AI, dating simulations, or technical tests, collected from a Korean online community. The benchmark focuses on identifying conversation types and user testing purposes to improve chatbot resilience against adversarial attacks.

safe_child_llm.specs: Text (Adversarial prompts split by age group)
safe_child_llm.description: A comprehensive benchmark and dataset for systematically assessing LLM safety across two developmental stages: children (7-12) and adolescents (13-17). It includes adversarial prompts curated from red-teaming corpora and human-annotated labels for jailbreak success and ethical refusal.

agent_red_teaming.item_count: Curated set of high-impact attacks (derived from 1.8M submissions)
agent_red_teaming.specs: Direct and indirect prompt injection attacks, real-world deployment scenarios
agent_red_teaming.description: A curated benchmark derived from a large-scale public red-teaming competition, designed to systematically evaluate the security robustness of LLM-powered agents against adversarial misuse and prompt injection in realistic scenarios.

ct_rate.specs: 3D Chest CT volumes, Text (Radiology Reports), Multi-abnormality labels
ct_rate.description: A large-scale 3D medical imaging dataset that pairs non-contrast chest CT volumes with corresponding radiology text reports. It is designed to address the scarcity of comprehensive 3D medical datasets and enables the development of foundation models like CT-CLIP and CT-CHAT for tasks such as zero-shot abnormality detection and report generation.

ct_rate_jp.description: A multilingual adaptation of the CT-RATE dataset, consisting of radiology reports translated into Japanese. It was created to facilitate the development of specialized Japanese medical language models and includes a subset of radiologist-revised reports for validation.

generatect_dataset.description: A synthetic dataset generated using the GenerateCT framework, consisting of chest CT volumes and corresponding text prompts. It serves as a benchmark for evaluating text-conditional 3D medical image generation capabilities.

pathmmu.description: A massive multimodal expert-level benchmark for understanding and reasoning in pathology. It serves as a comprehensive resource for evaluating Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) in the pathology domain, featuring expert-validated QA pairs derived from authoritative sources.

medexqa.description: A medical question-answering benchmark that includes multiple explanations for each answer to evaluate LLMs' understanding. While broad, it specifically covers underrepresented domains such as Speech Language Pathology.

wsi_path_align.item_count: Single WSI examples (count unspecified in snippet)
wsi_path_align.description: A dataset referenced in the development of MedGemma, consisting of de-identified H&E Whole Slide Images (WSIs) paired with associated final diagnosis text from original pathology reports. Used for training multimodal medical AI models.

ucf_multiorgan_path.specs: Whole Slide Images (WSI), Patches (512x512), 15 Organ Classes
ucf_multiorgan_path.description: A public benchmark dataset for multi-organ histopathologic image classification. Collected from cadavers over a decade, it addresses the limitations of existing datasets by providing a diverse collection of WSIs from 15 distinct organ classes (e.g., lung, kidney, liver, pancreas). It supports both patch-level and slide-level classification tasks.

dermavqa.description: An extension of the DermaVQA dataset that supports closed-ended question answering and dermatological lesion segmentation. It introduces the Dermatology Assessment Schema (DAS) for structured assessment.

medec.specs: Text (Clinical notes with annotated errors and corrections)
medec.description: A benchmark for medical error detection and correction in clinical notes. It covers five types of errors (Diagnosis, Management, Treatment, Pharmacotherapy, and Causal Organism) to assess the ability of LLMs to validate clinical text.

ehrxqa.specs: Multi-modal (Structured Tables + Chest X-ray Images); Text, Image, SQL
ehrxqa.description: A multi-modal question answering dataset that combines structured Electronic Health Records (EHR) from MIMIC-IV with chest X-ray images from MIMIC-CXR. It requires models to perform joint reasoning across both tabular and imaging modalities to answer clinical questions.

ehrsql.description: A large-scale text-to-SQL dataset for Electronic Health Records, designed to test QA models on structured data. It includes questions collected from hospital staff and covers a wide range of SQL queries, including those requiring time expression understanding and unanswerable question detection.

radimagenet_vqa.description: A large-scale synthetic dataset designed for training and benchmarking radiologic VQA on CT and MRI exams. It is built from the RadImageNet dataset with generated QA pairs to challenge multimodal models.

radgraph2.description: A dataset extending RadGraph to model disease progression in radiology reports. It utilizes a hierarchical schema to capture entities and relations, specifically focusing on changes in disease state and device placement over time compared to prior reports.

mimic_sql.description: A dataset for text-to-SQL generation on Electronic Medical Records. It consists of two subsets: machine-generated template questions and human-annotated natural language questions, based on MIMIC-III data.

mimic_sparql.description: A knowledge graph-based question answering dataset for EHRs. It is a counterpart to MIMIC-SQL, where the relational database is converted into a directed acyclic graph, and questions are mapped to SPARQL queries.

mimic_iv_labevents.description: A freely accessible electronic health record dataset containing de-identified clinical data of patients admitted to the ICU and Emergency Department at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. It includes vital signs, laboratory measurements, medications, and free-text clinical notes.

fastmri.description: An extension of the fastMRI dataset containing clinical pathology annotations (bounding boxes and labels) for knee and brain data.

fastmri_plus.description: An extension of the fastMRI dataset containing clinical pathology annotations (bounding boxes and labels) for knee and brain data.

object_cxr.specs: 5000 positive and 5000 negative samples, bounding boxes/masks
object_cxr.description: A benchmark dataset designed for the automatic detection of foreign objects in chest X-rays.

us_derm_mcqa.description: A dermatology multiple-choice question assessment benchmark often referenced in Google/DeepMind research (e.g., MedGemma). It is an internal dataset derived from the work of Liu et al. (2020), consisting of de-identified teledermatology cases with 136 skin conditions transformed into 4-way MCQs.

pharmaconer.specs: Text (Spanish clinical case reports with NER annotations)
pharmaconer.description: A benchmark track for Named Entity Recognition (NER) of pharmacological substances, compounds, and proteins in Spanish clinical cases, essential for pharmacovigilance and patient safety monitoring in non-English texts.

chestxray14.specs: Frontal-view X-ray images, 14 disease labels text-mined from reports
chestxray14.description: A hospital-scale chest X-ray database for weakly-supervised classification and localization of common thorax diseases.

breakhis.description: A benchmark for the classification of breast cancer histopathology images. The dataset contains microscopic images of breast tumor tissue collected from patients, labeled as either benign or malignant.

eyepacs_dr.specs: JPEG images, 5-class grading (0-4), high-resolution fundus photography
eyepacs_dr.description: A large-scale dataset of high-resolution retinal fundus images used for the automated detection of diabetic retinopathy. It was originally released as part of a Kaggle competition to identify the presence of diabetic retinopathy in images.

iu_xray.description: A collection of chest X-ray images with associated radiology reports from the Indiana University hospital network. It is widely used as a smaller benchmark for report generation.

pubhealth.specs: Public health claims, explanation text, veracity labels (True, False, Unproven, Mixture)
pubhealth.description: A comprehensive dataset for explainable automated fact-checking of public health claims. Each instance includes a veracity label and a journalist-crafted explanation.

healthslm_bench.specs: Text/Sensor Data; 8 health prediction tasks; Classification and Regression
healthslm_bench.description: A benchmark designed to systematically evaluate Small Language Models (SLMs) on mobile and wearable healthcare monitoring tasks. It covers zero-shot, few-shot, and instruction-tuned settings for health prediction tasks using sensor data.

imed_361m.description: A large-scale benchmark for interactive medical image segmentation. It features a massive collection of medical images with dense, interactive masks generated and verified using foundation models to simulate human-in-the-loop annotation workflows.

medsegbench.description: A comprehensive benchmark specifically designed for medical image segmentation, aggregating diverse datasets to evaluate model generalization across different medical imaging modalities.

sa_med2d_20m.specs: 2D Medical Images (CT, MRI, X-ray, Ultrasound, etc.), Mask annotations
sa_med2d_20m.description: A large-scale 2D medical image segmentation dataset designed to incorporate medical knowledge into the Segment Anything Model (SAM). It covers diverse modalities (CT, MRI, etc.) and anatomical structures.

atom3d_psr.item_count: ~5.3 TB (total ATOM3D volume), PSR specific: ~8 GB (raw), ~2 GB (split)
atom3d_psr.specs: LMDB format; Modalities: 3D Atomic Coordinates, Quality Scores
atom3d_psr.description: A benchmark task within the ATOM3D suite focused on predicting the quality (GDT_TS score) of protein structure models. It uses historical data from CASP competitions (CASP 5-13) to train and evaluate ranking methods.

sair_ic50.item_count: 5 million AI-generated 3D structures with potency labels
sair_ic50.description: A large-scale dataset of co-folded 3D protein-ligand structures paired with experimentally measured IC50 labels to link molecular structure directly to drug potency.

bipia.bmt_title: BIPIA (Benchmark for Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks)
bipia.description: The first benchmark designed to evaluate the robustness of Large Language Models against indirect prompt injection attacks, covering tasks like email QA, web QA, and summarization.

mol_instructions.specs: Text and Sequence-based (SMILES, Protein Sequences); Instruction Tuning format
mol_instructions.description: A comprehensive instruction tuning dataset for the biomolecular domain, designed to improve LLMs' understanding of biomolecules. It includes tasks related to small molecules, proteins, and biomolecular text.

eisost.description: A dataset for Sim-to-Real domain adaptation in medical imaging, specifically for the segmentation of oropharyngeal organs (uvula, epiglottis, glottis).

nyu_breast_path_ner.description: A dataset of breast pathology reports annotated for Named Entity Recognition (NER) tasks. It focuses on extracting key diagnostic elements such as cancer subtype, cancer grade, and lesion position from free-text clinical reports.

swe_bench_multilingual.description: An official extension of SWE-bench covering multiple programming languages to evaluate cross-lingual software engineering capabilities.

swe_bench_multimodal.description: An extension of SWE-bench designed to evaluate AI systems on their ability to fix bugs in visual, user-facing JavaScript software. Issues include visual elements like screenshots and diagrams.

charxiv_reasoning_no_tools.specs: Images (scientific charts), Text (questions and answers); Includes descriptive and reasoning question types
charxiv_reasoning_no_tools.description: A comprehensive evaluation suite designed to assess Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) on realistic chart understanding. It features 2,323 diverse and challenging charts sourced from arXiv papers across various scientific disciplines. The benchmark includes two types of questions: descriptive questions that test basic element recognition, and reasoning questions that require synthesizing complex visual information.

charxiv_reasoning_tools.specs: Images (scientific charts), Text (questions and answers); Includes descriptive and reasoning question types
charxiv_reasoning_tools.description: A comprehensive evaluation suite designed to assess Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) on realistic chart understanding. It features 2,323 diverse and challenging charts sourced from arXiv papers across various scientific disciplines. The benchmark includes two types of questions: descriptive questions that test basic element recognition, and reasoning questions that require synthesizing complex visual information.

hle_no_tools.description: A multi-modal, expert-level benchmark designed to be the final closed-ended academic evaluation for Large Language Models. It consists of difficult questions across dozens of subjects (mathematics, humanities, natural sciences) that current frontier models struggle to answer, constructed to test reasoning at the frontier of human knowledge.

hle_tools.description: A multi-modal, expert-level benchmark designed to be the final closed-ended academic evaluation for Large Language Models. It consists of difficult questions across dozens of subjects (mathematics, humanities, natural sciences) that current frontier models struggle to answer, constructed to test reasoning at the frontier of human knowledge.

gpqa_diamond.bmt_title: GPQA: A Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A Benchmark
gpqa_diamond.description: GPQA is a challenging multiple-choice question answering dataset written by domain experts in biology, physics, and chemistry. It is designed to be difficult even for highly skilled non-experts with unrestricted access to the internet (Google-proof), while domain experts can answer them with high accuracy.

swe_bench_verified.description: A human-validated subset of SWE-bench, consisting of 500 samples verified to be non-problematic and solvable by human software engineers. Developed in collaboration with OpenAI.

mmlu_pro.description: An enhanced dataset designed to extend the MMLU benchmark by integrating more challenging, reasoning-focused questions and expanding the choice set from four to ten options to reduce random guessing.

hle.description: A multi-modal, expert-level benchmark designed to be the final closed-ended academic evaluation for Large Language Models. It consists of difficult questions across dozens of subjects (mathematics, humanities, natural sciences) that current frontier models struggle to answer, constructed to test reasoning at the frontier of human knowledge.

arc_agi_2.item_count: Expanded set of tasks (exact count not specified in initial release)
arc_agi_2.description: An upgraded version of the ARC benchmark designed to provide finer-grained evaluation at higher levels of cognitive complexity. It maintains the same format as ARC-AGI-1 but introduces a curated set of tasks that are harder for current AI systems while remaining accessible to human intelligence.

aime_2026.specs: Text modality; LaTeX format; Includes problem type and ground-truth answers
aime_2026.description: A dataset containing questions from the AIME 2025 competition, created as part of the MathArena framework to evaluate LLMs on uncontaminated, newly released mathematical problems.

aime_2025.specs: Text modality; LaTeX format; Includes problem type and ground-truth answers
aime_2025.description: A dataset containing questions from the AIME 2025 competition, created as part of the MathArena framework to evaluate LLMs on uncontaminated, newly released mathematical problems.

bbh.description: A subset of the BIG-Bench suite, focusing on 23 challenging tasks where prior language models did not outperform the average human-rater. It emphasizes multi-step reasoning capabilities.

tau2_bench.specs: Dual-control simulation (Dec-POMDP); Domains: Retail, Airline, Telecom; Modalities: Text, API tools
tau2_bench.description: An enhanced version of Tau-bench that introduces a dual-control environment where both the agent and the user can interact with tools. It adds a 'Telecom' domain for technical troubleshooting and includes code fixes for previous domains.

terminal_bench_2.specs: Terminal-based tasks, Docker environments, Python/Bash execution harness
terminal_bench_2.description: A benchmark for benchmarking agents on hard, realistic tasks in command line interfaces (CLI). It evaluates how well agents can handle real-world, end-to-end tasks autonomously, ranging from compiling code to training models and setting up servers. The benchmark consists of a dataset of tasks and an execution harness connecting the agent to a terminal sandbox.

browsecomp.bmt_title: BrowseComp: A Simple Yet Challenging Benchmark for Browsing Agents
browsecomp.specs: Web browsing, information seeking, short answer
browsecomp.description: A benchmark for measuring the ability of agents to persistently navigate the internet in search of hard-to-find, entangled information. It parallels programming competitions by focusing on difficult, fact-seeking questions with short, verifiable answers.

lmarena.specs: Text conversations, Pairwise preference votes, JSON
lmarena.description: An open platform for evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) based on human preferences. It uses a crowdsourced, pairwise comparison approach where users chat with two anonymous models and vote on the better response, generating a leaderboard via the Bradley-Terry model.

osworld.description: A manually annotated version of the OSWorld benchmark containing human-determined trajectories for each task. It is designed to evaluate the efficiency (latency and step count) of computer-use agents compared to human performance.

osworld_verified.specs: Verified tasks, AWS integration, improved robustness
osworld_verified.description: An enhanced and verified version of the original OSWorld benchmark, featuring comprehensive bug fixes, improved infrastructure support (AWS), and refined task definitions to ensure reliable evaluation signals.

video_mme.specs: Videos range from short (11s) to long (1h); covers 6 domains (knowledge, film, sports, etc.); includes subtitles and audio.
video_mme.description: The first comprehensive benchmark for multi-modal evaluation in video analysis, covering diverse domains and video durations.

mmmu_pro.specs: Multimodal (Image/Screenshot), Multiple Choice (10 options), Vision-only input setting
mmmu_pro.description: A robust version of the MMMU benchmark designed to rigorously assess true multimodal understanding. It filters out text-only answerable questions, augments candidate options to 10 choices, and introduces a vision-only input setting (screenshots) to test the integration of visual and textual information.

mmmlu.description: A multilingual version of the MMLU benchmark, translated into 14 languages (including Yoruba, Swahili, etc.) using professional human translators to evaluate LLM performance across diverse linguistic contexts.

frontiermath.description: A benchmark for evaluating advanced mathematical reasoning in AI, featuring hundreds of original, expert-crafted mathematics problems that span major branches of modern mathematics and typically require hours or days for expert mathematicians to solve. The problems are kept unpublished to prevent contamination.

frontiermath_t4.description: A benchmark for evaluating advanced mathematical reasoning in AI, featuring hundreds of original, expert-crafted mathematics problems that span major branches of modern mathematics and typically require hours or days for expert mathematicians to solve. The problems are kept unpublished to prevent contamination.

longbench_v2.specs: Text; Multilingual (English, Chinese); Tasks range from 5k to 15k+ tokens; Includes NarrativeQA, Qasper, HotpotQA, etc.
longbench_v2.description: A comprehensive benchmark for long-context understanding, widely used to evaluate how well context pruning methods preserve performance on long sequences. It covers single/multi-doc QA, summarization, and few-shot learning.

livecodebench.specs: Code generation, self-repair, code execution, test output prediction tasks; Problems from LeetCode, AtCoder, CodeForces
livecodebench.description: LiveCodeBench is a holistic and contamination-free evaluation benchmark for Large Language Models (LLMs) for code. It continuously collects new problems from competitive programming contests (LeetCode, AtCoder, CodeForces) to prevent test set contamination. The benchmark assesses models on a broader range of code-related capabilities beyond just generation, including self-repair, code execution, and test output prediction.

super_gpqa.specs: Text (Multiple Choice Questions); Covers 285 graduate-level disciplines including light industry, agriculture, and service-oriented fields.
super_gpqa.description: A large-scale benchmark designed to evaluate the graduate-level knowledge and reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) across 285 specialized disciplines. It employs a human-LLM collaborative filtering mechanism for quality assurance.

cybench.specs: CTF challenges involving file analysis, network interactions, and cryptography. Includes breakdown into subtasks for granular evaluation.
cybench.description: A benchmark for evaluating the cybersecurity capabilities and risks of language models. It includes professional-level Capture the Flag (CTF) tasks covering both offensive and defensive scenarios.

cvebench.specs: Video samples, human preference scores (MOS). Diverse content including real-world, AIGC, and CG videos.
cvebench.description: A subjective-aligned benchmark suite for text-driven video editing quality assessment. It includes a database with rich video-prompt pairs and human scores to train a quality assessment model.

cybergym.specs: 1,507 historical vulnerabilities from 188 open-source software projects (e.g., OpenSSL, FFmpeg); Dockerized environments; Modalities: Text (descriptions), Code (C/C++).
cybergym.description: A large-scale, high-quality cybersecurity evaluation framework and benchmark designed to rigorously assess the capabilities of AI agents on real-world vulnerability analysis tasks. It provides an execution-based evaluation environment where agents must generate proof-of-concept (PoC) tests to reproduce vulnerabilities given a description and code.

airtbench.specs: Text/Code (Python); Black-box CTF challenges; Interaction traces
airtbench.description: A benchmark measuring autonomous AI red teaming capabilities in language models. It consists of 70 realistic black-box capture-the-flag (CTF) challenges from the Crucible environment, requiring models to write Python code to autonomously discover and exploit AI/ML security vulnerabilities. The release includes both the challenge framework and a dataset of over 8,000 experimental run traces.

autopatchbench.specs: C/C++, Fuzzing-identified vulnerabilities, Automated patch generation
autopatchbench.description: A benchmark for assessing the capabilities of automated patch generation systems on real-world vulnerabilities identified through fuzzing. It is part of the CyberSecEval suite and focuses on security fixes for C/C++ code.

baxbench.specs: Multi-language (Python, JS, Go, etc.), Backend frameworks, End-to-end exploits
baxbench.description: A comprehensive, manually-curated benchmark for evaluating the security and correctness of backend code generation. It covers a wide range of frameworks and vulnerability types, serving as a high-quality baseline for automated bootstrapping approaches like AutoBaxBuilder.

gaia.specs: Text questions, varying modalities (images, files), Tool use required
gaia.description: A benchmark for General AI Assistants featuring conceptually simple questions for humans that are challenging for AI. It requires fundamental abilities such as reasoning, tool use, and multi-modality to solve real-world tasks.

tau_bench.specs: Dynamic conversation simulation; Domains: Retail, Airline; Modalities: Text (dialogue), API calls
tau_bench.description: A benchmark emulating dynamic conversations between a user (simulated by a language model) and a language agent provided with domain-specific API tools and policy guidelines. It focuses on evaluating tool usage, reasoning, and policy adherence in real-world scenarios.

dfir_metric.specs: Disk images, memory blocks, file system parsing tasks, Python script generation prompts
dfir_metric.description: A benchmark dataset tailored for evaluating LLMs in Digital Forensics and Incident Response (DFIR). It adapts tasks from the NIST Computer Forensics Tool Testing Program to assess capabilities in file system analysis, timeline reconstruction, and recovering active/deleted files, directly relating to system integrity verification.

mcp_atlas.specs: 36 MCP servers, 220 tools, Parquet/CSV format, Text modality
mcp_atlas.description: A large-scale benchmark for evaluating tool-use competency with real MCP servers. It tests agents on realistic, multi-step workflows involving tool discovery, parameterization, and error recovery, comprising 1,000 human-authored tasks (500 public) across 36 servers.

vending_bench_2.specs: Multi-agent competitive environment (Arena); Adversarial supplier simulation; Negotiation and strategy evaluation
vending_bench_2.description: An evolution of the original Vending-Bench that introduces a competitive 'Arena' mode and more realistic challenges. In this version, agents must manage their vending machine business for a full simulated year while dealing with adversarial suppliers, price wars with other agents, and complex negotiation scenarios. It is designed to test long-horizon planning, economic strategy, and robustness against exploitation.

webarena.specs: Web-based tasks, Text/HTML modality, Dockerized environments
webarena.description: A realistic and reproducible web environment for building and evaluating autonomous agents. It consists of fully functional websites from four common domains (e-commerce, social forums, software development, content management) to test agents on long-horizon web tasks.

deepsearchqa.specs: Text, Set-based answers; 17 domains (e.g., Finance, Science, Politics).
deepsearchqa.description: A benchmark for evaluating agents on difficult multi-step information-seeking tasks across 17 fields, designed to assess an agent's ability to execute complex search plans and generate exhaustive answer lists (addressing the 'comprehensiveness gap').

gdpval_aa.specs: Text and file deliverables (documents, spreadsheets, slides); 44 occupations.
gdpval_aa.description: A benchmark evaluating AI model capabilities on real-world economically valuable tasks. It covers 44 occupations across key sectors contributing to US GDP. GDPval-AA is Artificial Analysis' evaluation framework for OpenAI's GDPval dataset.

matharena_apex.specs: LaTeX format; problems sourced from various 2025 math competitions; strict output format evaluation
matharena_apex.description: A benchmark evaluating Large Language Models on uncontaminated, extremely challenging math competition problems from 2025. It focuses on 'Apex' problems where even state-of-the-art models struggle, ensuring a rigorous test of mathematical reasoning.

screenspot_pro.specs: High-resolution screenshots, bounding box annotations, natural language instructions; covers 23 applications across 5 industries.
screenspot_pro.description: A benchmark designed to rigorously evaluate the GUI grounding capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in high-resolution professional settings. It focuses on authentic tasks within professional applications (e.g., coding, design) rather than general web browsing.

charxiv_reasoning.specs: Images (scientific charts), Text (questions and answers); Includes descriptive and reasoning question types
charxiv_reasoning.description: A comprehensive evaluation suite designed to assess Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) on realistic chart understanding. It features 2,323 diverse and challenging charts sourced from arXiv papers across various scientific disciplines. The benchmark includes two types of questions: descriptive questions that test basic element recognition, and reasoning questions that require synthesizing complex visual information.

omnidocbench.specs: PDF documents, 19 layout categories, 14 attribute labels; covers 9 document types.
omnidocbench.description: A diverse and comprehensive benchmark for document parsing and content extraction. It addresses limitations in existing datasets by including nine distinct document types (e.g., academic papers, textbooks, handwritten notes) and providing fine-grained annotations for layout analysis and attributes.

video_mmmu.specs: Video + Text, 6 professional disciplines, 30 subjects, lecture-style videos
video_mmmu.description: A multi-modal, multi-disciplinary benchmark evaluating Large Multimodal Models' (LMMs) ability to acquire and utilize knowledge from educational videos. It assesses performance across three cognitive stages: Perception, Comprehension, and Adaptation.

facts_benchmark.specs: Text, Images, Search Tools; Split into Multimodal, Parametric, Search, and Grounding (v2) benchmarks.
facts_benchmark.description: A comprehensive benchmark suite evaluating the factuality of Large Language Models across four dimensions: Multimodal (image-based factuality), Parametric (internal knowledge), Search (using external tools), and Grounding (faithfulness to provided text).

simpleqa_verified.specs: Text modality; Verified short-form factuality questions
simpleqa_verified.description: A refined subset of OpenAI's SimpleQA designed to address limitations such as noisy labels, topical biases, and question redundancy. It employs a rigorous filtering process (deduplication, source reconciliation) to provide a more reliable measure of parametric knowledge.

global_piqa.item_count: 11,600 examples (100 examples per language for 116 languages)
global_piqa.specs: Multilingual text (116 languages); Multiple choice; Culturally specific physical reasoning
global_piqa.description: A large-scale multilingual benchmark for physical commonsense reasoning across over 100 languages and cultures. Unlike translation-based benchmarks, this dataset features culturally specific examples constructed by native speakers to evaluate how well LLMs capture global physical knowledge.

scicode.specs: Python code generation; covers 16 natural science subdomains.
scicode.description: A scientist-curated benchmark designed to evaluate the capabilities of language models in generating code for solving realistic scientific research problems.
