Problems are decomposed into subproblems involving knowledge recall, reasoning, and code synthesis across fields like Physics, Math, and Chemistry.

longvideobench.specs: Interleaved Video-Language; Videos up to 1 hour; Multiple Choice QA
longvideobench.description: A benchmark for long-context interleaved video-language understanding. It focuses on 'referring reasoning' tasks where the model must retrieve and reason over detailed multimodal information from videos up to an hour long. The dataset relies on web-collected videos with subtitles.

livecodebench_v6.specs: Code generation, self-repair, code execution, test output prediction tasks; Problems from LeetCode, AtCoder, CodeForces
livecodebench_v6.description: LiveCodeBench is a holistic and contamination-free evaluation benchmark for Large Language Models (LLMs) for code. It continuously collects new problems from competitive programming contests (LeetCode, AtCoder, CodeForces) to prevent test set contamination. The benchmark assesses models on a broader range of code-related capabilities beyond just generation, including self-repair, code execution, and test output prediction.

paperbench.specs: 20 ICML 2024 papers with hierarchical grading rubrics
paperbench.description: A benchmark evaluating the ability of AI agents to replicate state-of-the-art AI research papers from scratch. It requires agents to understand paper contributions, develop a codebase, and execute experiments to match published results.

mle_bench.specs: 75 offline Kaggle competitions (multimodal data including text, image, audio, tabular). Available in 'Full' (3.3 TB) and 'Lite' (158 GB) subsets.
mle_bench.description: A benchmark for evaluating AI agents on machine learning engineering tasks. It consists of 75 curated Kaggle competitions that test real-world skills such as training models, preparing datasets, and running experiments. Agents are evaluated by their ability to achieve medal-level performance on the competition leaderboards.

cyscenariobench.description: A scenario-based evaluation suite developed by Irregular to assess LLM cyber capabilities across full attack workflows. Unlike atomic task benchmarks, it models realistic operational conditions, testing orchestration, branching decisions, and recovery from state inconsistencies. It is used for external red-teaming of frontier models like GPT-5.3.

livecodebench_elo.specs: Code generation, self-repair, code execution, test output prediction tasks; Problems from LeetCode, AtCoder, CodeForces
livecodebench_elo.description: LiveCodeBench is a holistic and contamination-free evaluation benchmark for Large Language Models (LLMs) for code. It continuously collects new problems from competitive programming contests (LeetCode, AtCoder, CodeForces) to prevent test set contamination. The benchmark assesses models on a broader range of code-related capabilities beyond just generation, including self-repair, code execution, and test output prediction.

apex_agents.specs: Multi-turn, cross-application tasks within realistic 'worlds' (file systems, emails, calendars). Includes prompts, rubrics, gold outputs, and simulated environment assets.
apex_agents.description: The AI Productivity Index for Agents (APEX-Agents) evaluates whether AI agents can execute long-horizon, cross-application professional tasks. Tasks are designed by experts in investment banking, management consulting, and corporate law to mirror real-world workflows.

fortress.bmt_title: FORTRESS (Frontier Risk Evaluation for National Security and Public Safety)
fortress.item_count: 1,000 samples (500 adversarial, 500 benign) in public set
fortress.specs: Text (Parquet format); Domains: CBRNE, Political Violence, Criminal Activities
fortress.description: A red-teaming benchmark containing expert-crafted adversarial prompts and benign counterparts to evaluate LLM safeguards against CBRNE, terrorism, and criminal activity risks.

abc_bench.specs: Dockerized environments, 8 languages, 19 frameworks, end-to-end API tests
abc_bench.description: Evaluates agentic backend coding within a realistic, executable workflow. Unlike static code benchmarks, it requires agents to manage the full development lifecycle (repo exploration, environment config, deployment) in a sandbox, often allowing white-box analysis of the coding process.

webvoyager.description: A benchmark for end-to-end web agents powered by Large Multimodal Models (LMMs). It consists of real-world tasks from 15 popular websites and introduces an automatic evaluation protocol using GPT-4V to assess open-ended task completion.

windows_agent_arena.specs: Windows OS, Multimodal (Vision + Action), Scalable Cloud Evaluation
windows_agent_arena.description: A scalable Windows AI agent platform and benchmark for testing and benchmarking multi-modal, desktop AI agents. It provides a reproducible and realistic Windows OS environment where agents can be evaluated on a diverse range of tasks involving planning, screen understanding, and tool usage.

scienceagentbench.specs: Scientific data analysis, Python code generation, 44 peer-reviewed publications
scienceagentbench.description: A benchmark specifically designed to evaluate language agents for data-driven scientific discovery. It includes tasks extracted from peer-reviewed publications across multiple disciplines, validated by subject matter experts.

mcp_bench.description: A benchmark for evaluating LLMs on realistic, multi-step tasks that demand tool use, cross-tool coordination, and planning via MCP servers. It connects LLMs to 28 representative live MCP servers spanning 250 tools across domains like finance and science.

livemcpbench.description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate LLM agents in large-scale, real-world scenarios using the Model Context Protocol. It tests agents on their ability to navigate a large collection of tools ('an ocean of MCP tools') for daily tasks.

browsecomp_plus.specs: Fixed corpus of web documents; human-verified positive and hard-negative relevance judgments; multi-step reasoning tasks
browsecomp_plus.description: A benchmark designed to evaluate deep-research AI agents that integrate retrieval and multi-step reasoning. Unlike its predecessor BrowseComp, it uses a fixed, human-verified corpus to ensure fair and reproducible comparisons of retrieval and reasoning capabilities.

audiobench.specs: Text and Audio inputs/outputs; Covers Speech, Sound, Music
audiobench.description: A universal benchmark for Audio Large Language Models (AudioLLMs) evaluating speech understanding, audio scene understanding, and paralinguistic voice traits. It unifies evaluation across 8 tasks and 26 datasets.

cti_bench.specs: TSV/Text format; Includes MCQs, CVE to CWE mapping, Vulnerability Severity Prediction (CVSS), Attack Technique Extraction
cti_bench.description: A curated benchmark designed to evaluate LLMs on a diverse set of cyber threat intelligence (CTI) tasks, including knowledge, attribution, and severity analysis.

cybermetric.description: A comprehensive benchmark dataset comprising 10,000 questions sourced from cybersecurity standards, certifications, and research. While not exclusively for DoS, it provides a domain-specific baseline for evaluating LLM knowledge in cybersecurity, including attack concepts.

secrepobench.specs: C/C++ Repositories, Secret Detection, Code Completion
secrepobench.description: A repository-level benchmark framework for evaluating secure code generation and secret detection. It integrates the SecretBench dataset and real-world C/C++ vulnerabilities to assess model performance in practical, complex software contexts.

megavul.specs: C/C++ code, JSON format, graph representations
megavul.description: A large-scale, multi-dimensional C/C++ vulnerability dataset constructed from CVEs and open-source projects, offering comprehensive code representations.

blink.specs: 14 classic computer vision tasks reformatted as multiple-choice questions; tasks include relative depth, visual correspondence, and rotation.
blink.description: A benchmark focusing on core visual perception abilities (e.g., depth estimation, forensics, multi-view reasoning) that are easy for humans but hard for current MLLMs.

finance_agent.specs: Text, Financial Data, SEC Filings; 9 task categories.
finance_agent.description: A comprehensive evaluation framework testing whether AI agents can autonomously complete complex financial research tasks (e.g., market research, financial modeling) using tools like SEC filings and web search.

healthbench_hard.description: An open-source benchmark designed to measure the performance and safety of large language models in healthcare. It consists of realistic multi-turn conversations between a model and an individual user or healthcare professional, evaluating responses against conversation-specific rubrics created by physicians. The benchmark covers diverse themes such as emergency referrals, context-seeking, and global health.

healthbench_consensus.description: An open-source benchmark designed to measure the performance and safety of large language models in healthcare. It consists of realistic multi-turn conversations between a model and an individual user or healthcare professional, evaluating responses against conversation-specific rubrics created by physicians. The benchmark covers diverse themes such as emergency referrals, context-seeking, and global health.

supergpqa.specs: Text (Multiple Choice Questions); Covers 285 graduate-level disciplines including light industry, agriculture, and service-oriented fields.
supergpqa.description: A large-scale benchmark designed to evaluate the graduate-level knowledge and reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) across 285 specialized disciplines. It employs a human-LLM collaborative filtering mechanism for quality assurance.

zebralogic.description: A controlled benchmark consisting of logic grid puzzles (Zebra Puzzles) designed to evaluate the scaling limits and logical reasoning capabilities of LLMs with adjustable complexity.

livebench.description: A contamination-free benchmark for LLMs that updates its questions monthly to prevent overfitting, covering math, coding, reasoning, data analysis, and instruction following.

harmbench.description: A standardized evaluation framework for automated red teaming, systematically designed to meet criteria of breadth, comparability, and robust metrics. It includes a validation set of behaviors and methods for automated attacks.

strongreject.specs: Text prompts covering 6 categories of harmful behavior (e.g., Illegal goods, Violence, Disinformation); includes an automated evaluator.
strongreject.description: StrongREJECT is a benchmark designed to evaluate the susceptibility of Large Language Models (LLMs) to jailbreak attacks. It addresses the shortcomings of previous benchmarks by distinguishing between 'empty' jailbreaks (where models fail to refuse but provide no harmful info) and effective ones. The benchmark consists of a curated dataset of forbidden prompts and an automated evaluator that assesses both the refusal and the quality/specificity of the harmful response.

airbench.description: A comprehensive safety benchmark for Large Language Models that evaluates risks across multiple categories, including explicit risk scenarios defined by government regulations and corporate policies. It tests for both the recognition of safety issues and the refusal of harmful queries.

multi_swe_bench.specs: 8 Languages (Python, Java, TS, JS, Go, Rust, C, C++), Text + Code
multi_swe_bench.description: A large-scale multilingual benchmark for issue resolving, covering 8 major programming languages including Java, TypeScript, Go, and C++.

swe_polybench.specs: Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python; Repository-level tasks
swe_polybench.description: A multi-language benchmark for repository-level execution-based evaluation of coding agents, covering bug fixes, feature additions, and refactoring.

simplebench.description: A multiple-choice text benchmark designed to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) on tasks where unspecialized human performance (high school level) still exceeds that of frontier models. It includes over 200 questions covering spatio-temporal reasoning, social intelligence, and linguistic adversarial robustness (trick questions).

fiction_livebench.description: A contamination-free benchmark for LLMs that updates its questions monthly to prevent overfitting, covering math, coding, reasoning, data analysis, and instruction following.

agieval.specs: Text-based (mostly), Multiple Choice, Cloze. Bilingual (English and Chinese).
agieval.description: A human-centric benchmark derived from official, high-standard admission and qualification exams (e.g., SAT, Gaokao, LSAT) intended for human test-takers, assessing general abilities pertinent to human cognition.

mmlu_redux.description: A manually re-annotated subset of the MMLU dataset aimed at identifying and fixing errors (such as wrong ground truths) in the original benchmark to ensure more reliable model evaluation.

cmmlu.description: A comprehensive Chinese benchmark covering 67 subjects across natural science, social sciences, engineering, and humanities, designed to evaluate the knowledge and reasoning capabilities of LLMs in a Chinese context.

chinese_simpleqa.specs: Text modality; Short-form question answering; Single indisputable answer
chinese_simpleqa.description: A factuality benchmark that measures the ability of language models to answer short, fact-seeking questions. It focuses on high correctness and is designed to be challenging for frontier models (adversarially collected against GPT-4) while ensuring answers are easy to grade.

bigcodebench.specs: Python, Complex instructions, Tool use/Function calls
bigcodebench.description: A benchmark designed to assess code generation with complex instructions and diverse function calls. It aims to be more challenging than HumanEval by requiring the use of multiple libraries and tools.

mcpatlas_public.specs: 36 MCP servers, 220 tools, Parquet/CSV format, Text modality
mcpatlas_public.description: A large-scale benchmark for evaluating tool-use competency with real MCP servers. It tests agents on realistic, multi-step workflows involving tool discovery, parameterization, and error recovery, comprising 1,000 human-authored tasks (500 public) across 36 servers.

mcpmark.description: A benchmark designed to stress-test comprehensive MCP use in realistic scenarios. It includes tasks across Notion, GitHub, Filesystem, PostgreSQL, and Playwright environments, featuring high-quality tasks collaboratively created by human experts and AI agents.

qwen_web_bench.description: A large-scale benchmark designed to evaluate browser agents on realistic tasks across live websites. It distinguishes between READ (information extraction) and WRITE (actions like form filling) tasks to better quantify agent capabilities.

nl2repo.specs: Input: Natural language requirements; Output: Fully functional Python repository.
nl2repo.description: A benchmark explicitly designed to evaluate the long-horizon repository generation ability of coding agents. It requires agents to autonomously design architecture, manage dependencies, and implement multi-module logic from a single natural language requirement.

android_world.bmt_title: AndroidWorld: A Dynamic Benchmarking Environment for Autonomous Agents
android_world.specs: Android environment, dynamic task generation, reward signals
android_world.description: A fully functional Android environment that dynamically constructs parameterized tasks expressed in natural language, enabling testing on a large suite of tasks.

realworldqa.description: A diagnostic benchmark for evaluating multimodal world knowledge in video understanding models. It focuses on long-chain reasoning and includes questions requiring knowledge of societal norms, tool use, and physical interactions.

protocolqa_openended.description: A modification of the ProtocolQA dataset designed to evaluate the ability to troubleshoot commonly published lab protocols. The dataset modifies 108 multiple-choice questions from the original ProtocolQA to be open-ended short answer questions, introducing egregious errors in protocols and asking for fixes.

troubleshootingbench.specs: Text-based; Short-answer troubleshooting questions based on expert-written biological protocols
troubleshootingbench.description: A benchmark designed to evaluate large language models' ability to identify and correct real-world experimental errors in biological protocols (wet lab procedures). It focuses on tacit, hands-on knowledge and uncontaminated procedures that are not available online, requiring models to troubleshoot complex, domain-specific scenarios.

haerae.description: A benchmark designed to evaluate Korean knowledge in language models, focusing on cultural and linguistic nuances that are often lost in translation-based benchmarks. It covers domains like vocabulary, history, general knowledge, and reading comprehension.

komt_bench.description: A set of 80 high-quality multi-turn questions designed to test the conversation flow and instruction-following capabilities of LLMs. It uses GPT-4 as a judge to evaluate model responses against a reference.

k_mmbench.specs: Multiple-choice questions covering 20 ability dimensions arranged in a hierarchy (Perception, Reasoning, etc.); uses CircularEval to test consistency.
k_mmbench.description: A comprehensive evaluation pipeline for large vision-language models using 'CircularEval' to assess robustness across perception and reasoning abilities.

mathvista.specs: Derived from 28 existing datasets and 3 new ones (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA); covers geometry, charts, and function plots.
mathvista.description: A benchmark specifically designed to evaluate mathematical reasoning in visual contexts, combining diverse mathematical and visual tasks.

mt_bench.description: A set of 80 high-quality multi-turn questions designed to test the conversation flow and instruction-following capabilities of LLMs. It uses GPT-4 as a judge to evaluate model responses against a reference.

skild_failure_recovery.description: A multimodal repository for COVID-19 news credibility research. It combines news articles with their social spread on Twitter, including visual and temporal information to aid in credibility assessment.

nyu_ctf.specs: CTF Challenges (Dockerized); Modalities: Text, Code, Binary Interaction
nyu_ctf.description: A scalable, open-source benchmark dataset designed to evaluate LLMs in offensive security. It features verified CTF challenges hosted in Docker containers to test agents' task planning and vulnerability exploitation skills.

docvqa.description: A dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images, containing questions defined on a wide variety of document types.

chartqa.description: A benchmark for Question Answering about charts requiring visual and logical reasoning. It combines human-authored question-answer pairs with machine-generated ones to cover a wide range of visual and logical reasoning tasks.

repobench.description: A benchmark designed for evaluating repository-level code auto-completion systems. It evaluates retrieval, code completion, and pipeline tasks with cross-file context.

libero.description: A benchmark for lifelong robot learning, focusing on knowledge transfer across tasks. It includes task suites designed to test declarative and procedural knowledge transfer under distribution shifts.

robocasa.specs: MuJoCo Simulation, RGB-D observations, Language descriptions, Generative AI-augmented assets
robocasa.description: A large-scale simulation framework for training generalist robots, featuring realistic and diverse kitchen environments populated with assets generated by generative AI tools. It focuses on everyday tasks to scale up robot learning data.

robotwin2.specs: Synthetic data, dual-arm manipulation, 5 robot embodiments, 731 object assets (RoboTwin-OD)
robotwin2.description: A scalable simulation framework and benchmark for bimanual robotic manipulation. It utilizes a multimodal large language model (MLLM) pipeline for automated task generation and incorporates strong domain randomization (lighting, clutter, etc.) to produce diverse synthetic data for sim-to-real transfer.

vlabench.specs: Simulation-based, Language-Conditioned Manipulation (LCM), Multi-step reasoning tasks
vlabench.description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate Vision-Language-Action models on language-conditioned manipulation tasks, focusing on long-horizon reasoning, world knowledge transfer, and implicit human intentions.

open_x_embodiment.specs: RLDS format (serialized tfrecords), RGB images, Depth, Point Clouds, Natural Language Instructions, Robot Actions (7-DOF)
open_x_embodiment.description: A massive robotics dataset aggregating over 1 million real-world robot trajectories from 22 different robot embodiments to facilitate cross-embodiment learning and the training of generalist robot policies.

afrimed_qa.specs: Includes 4,000+ expert Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs), 1,200+ Open-Ended Short Answer Questions (SAQs), and 10,000 Consumer Queries (CQs). Covers 32 medical specialties across 16 African countries.
afrimed_qa.description: A large-scale Pan-African, multi-specialty medical Question-Answering (QA) benchmark dataset designed to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) in the context of African healthcare. The dataset aims to address the underrepresentation of African health data in LLM training and evaluation, covering diverse geographic and clinical contexts.

hellaswag.description: An adversarial dataset for commonsense natural language inference where models must select the best ending to a context, designed to be hard for state-of-the-art models.

humaneval_plus.specs: Python functions with docstrings and unit tests
humaneval_plus.description: A benchmark for evaluating the functional correctness of code generated by Large Language Models. It consists of programming problems that include a function signature, docstring, body, and unit tests.

cruxeval.description: A benchmark dedicated to evaluating code reasoning, understanding, and execution. It consists of Python functions with input-output pairs, requiring models to predict the output given an input (execution) or the input given an output (reverse execution).

aime_24.specs: JSONL format; Text modality; Integer answers (0-999)
aime_24.description: A benchmark dataset consisting of 30 problems from the 2024 American Invitational Mathematics Examination (AIME I and II). It is widely used to evaluate the mathematical reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) on difficult, Olympiad-level problems.

mathvista_mini.specs: Derived from 28 existing datasets and 3 new ones (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA); covers geometry, charts, and function plots.
mathvista_mini.description: A benchmark specifically designed to evaluate mathematical reasoning in visual contexts, combining diverse mathematical and visual tasks.

mmbench_en.specs: Multiple-choice questions covering 20 ability dimensions arranged in a hierarchy (Perception, Reasoning, etc.); uses CircularEval to test consistency.
mmbench_en.description: A comprehensive evaluation pipeline for large vision-language models using 'CircularEval' to assess robustness across perception and reasoning abilities.

mtbench.description: A set of 80 high-quality multi-turn questions designed to test the conversation flow and instruction-following capabilities of LLMs. It uses GPT-4 as a judge to evaluate model responses against a reference.

mimic_cxr_f1.specs: DICOM/JPG images, free-text radiology reports, 14 CheXpert-derived labels
mimic_cxr_f1.description: A large publicly available dataset of chest radiographs with free-text radiology reports, de-identified and sourced from the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center.

dermmcqa.description: A dermatology multiple-choice question assessment benchmark often referenced in Google/DeepMind research (e.g., MedGemma). It is an internal dataset derived from the work of Liu et al. (2020), consisting of de-identified teledermatology cases with 136 skin conditions transformed into 4-way MCQs.

robocasa365.specs: MuJoCo Simulation, RGB-D observations, Language descriptions, Generative AI-augmented assets
robocasa365.description: A large-scale simulation framework for training generalist robots, featuring realistic and diverse kitchen environments populated with assets generated by generative AI tools. It focuses on everyday tasks to scale up robot learning data.

robovqa.description: A large-scale dataset for multimodal long-horizon reasoning in robotics. It contains video-text pairs from recordings of long-horizon instructions performed by robots and humans, used as a component in PhyCritic-Bench.

physical_ai_bench.specs: Video, Text; Categories include Robotic Arm Operations, Autonomous Driving, Ego-centric Life
physical_ai_bench.description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate perception and prediction capabilities across video generation, conditional video generation, and video understanding. It comprises real-world cases with task-aligned metrics to capture physical plausibility and domain-specific reasoning.

humanoid_failure_recovery_time.description: A multimodal repository for COVID-19 news credibility research. It combines news articles with their social spread on Twitter, including visual and temporal information to aid in credibility assessment.

aime_2024.specs: JSONL format; Text modality; Integer answers (0-999)
aime_2024.description: A benchmark dataset consisting of 30 problems from the 2024 American Invitational Mathematics Examination (AIME I and II). It is widely used to evaluate the mathematical reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) on difficult, Olympiad-level problems.

sea_helm.bmt_title: SEA-HELM (Southeast Asian Holistic Evaluation of Language Models)
sea_helm.item_count: 5 core pillars covering various datasets (including SEA-IFEval, SEA-MTBench, LINDSEA, Kalahi)
sea_helm.specs: Text modality; Languages: Filipino, Indonesian, Tamil, Thai, Vietnamese
sea_helm.description: A comprehensive and holistic benchmark suite designed to evaluate the linguistic and cultural competencies of Large Language Models (LLMs) in Southeast Asian languages. It comprises five core pillars: NLP Classics, LLM-specifics, SEA Linguistics, SEA Culture, and Safety.

superqpga.specs: Text (Multiple Choice Questions); Covers 285 graduate-level disciplines including light industry, agriculture, and service-oriented fields.
superqpga.description: A large-scale benchmark designed to evaluate the graduate-level knowledge and reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) across 285 specialized disciplines. It employs a human-LLM collaborative filtering mechanism for quality assurance.

worldscore_static.specs: 3D/4D Scene Generation, Video Generation, Consistency metrics
worldscore_static.description: A unified evaluation benchmark for world generation models (3D/4D scenes and video). It measures the consistency and quality of generated worlds, differentiating between superficial visual quality and structural world coherence.

worldscore_dynamic.specs: 3D/4D Scene Generation, Video Generation, Consistency metrics
worldscore_dynamic.description: A unified evaluation benchmark for world generation models (3D/4D scenes and video). It measures the consistency and quality of generated worlds, differentiating between superficial visual quality and structural world coherence.

worldscore_3d_consistency.specs: 3D/4D Scene Generation, Video Generation, Consistency metrics
worldscore_3d_consistency.description: A unified evaluation benchmark for world generation models (3D/4D scenes and video). It measures the consistency and quality of generated worlds, differentiating between superficial visual quality and structural world coherence.

vlabench_track1_primitive.specs: Simulation-based, Language-Conditioned Manipulation (LCM), Multi-step reasoning tasks
vlabench_track1_primitive.description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate Vision-Language-Action models on language-conditioned manipulation tasks, focusing on long-horizon reasoning, world knowledge transfer, and implicit human intentions.

worldmodelbench_avg.description: A benchmark designed to evaluate the world modeling capabilities of video generation models in application-driven domains like robotics and autonomous driving. It assesses models on instruction following, physical consistency (e.g., Newton's laws), and commonsense plausibility using a fine-tuned judger model.

simpler_env_avg.specs: Simulation (ManiSkill2 engine), Visual Matching evaluation, Real-to-Sim validation
simpler_env_avg.description: A benchmark suite for evaluating manipulation policies in simulation (using ManiSkill2) that correlates strongly with real-world performance on Google Robot and WidowX embodiments, aiming to mitigate the Sim-to-Real gap in evaluation.

meds_bench.item_count: Derived from 28 datasets (Total size varies by subset)
meds_bench.specs: Text; 11 Clinical Task Categories (QA, Summarization, NER, Diagnosis, etc.)
meds_bench.description: A comprehensive benchmark spanning 11 high-level clinical task categories (e.g., diagnosis, treatment planning, summarization) derived from 28 existing datasets, reformatted into instruction-prompted QA.

mmedbench.specs: Multilingual QA (English, Chinese, Japanese, French, Russian, Spanish); Text
mmedbench.description: A multilingual medical benchmark designed to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) on medical question answering and reasoning across six different languages.

medbench_cn.specs: Text (Chinese medical exams, clinical cases), QA
medbench_cn.description: A large-scale comprehensive benchmark for evaluating Chinese medical Large Language Models (LLMs). It covers 43 clinical specialties and includes questions from medical licensing exams, resident training exams, and real-world clinical cases.

echonet_lvef_mae.specs: Echocardiogram videos, measurements (EF, LV volume), tracings
echonet_lvef_mae.description: A large video dataset of echocardiograms for assessing cardiac function, including labels for ejection fraction, left ventricular volume, and expert tracings.

open_medical_llm_avg.item_count: Aggregates multiple datasets (MedQA, MedMCQA, PubMedQA, MMLU-Medical)
open_medical_llm_avg.description: A standardized leaderboard and evaluation suite hosted on Hugging Face that aggregates multiple datasets (MedQA, PubMedQA, MedMCQA, etc.) to track and rank the performance of Large Language Models on medical tasks.

jmedbench.specs: Text (Chinese medical exams, clinical cases), QA
jmedbench.description: A large-scale comprehensive benchmark for evaluating Chinese medical Large Language Models (LLMs). It covers 43 clinical specialties and includes questions from medical licensing exams, resident training exams, and real-world clinical cases.

swe_bench_verified_mini.description: A human-validated subset of SWE-bench, consisting of 500 samples verified to be non-problematic and solvable by human software engineers. Developed in collaboration with OpenAI.

simplerenv.specs: Simulation (ManiSkill2 engine), Visual Matching evaluation, Real-to-Sim validation
simplerenv.description: A benchmark suite for evaluating manipulation policies in simulation (using ManiSkill2) that correlates strongly with real-world performance on Google Robot and WidowX embodiments, aiming to mitigate the Sim-to-Real gap in evaluation.

matharena_arxivlean.specs: Text (LaTeX math problems), visual elements (diagrams in some subsets like Kangaroo), proof-based and short-answer modalities.
matharena_arxivlean.description: MathArena is a dynamic benchmark designed to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) on newly released mathematical competitions to prevent data contamination. It aggregates problems from various high-level competitions (e.g., AIME, IMO, CMIMC) immediately after they are held. The benchmark uniquely includes both final-answer format problems and proof-based problems (such as those from the IMO), requiring models to generate full reasoning chains. It aims to provide a rigorous, forward-looking assessment of mathematical reasoning and proof-writing capabilities.
